Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The umpires are out in the middle followed by the players of India led by Harmanpreet Kaur. Hayley Matthews walks out along with Qiana Joseph as the openers for West Indies Women. Renuka Singh Thakur will bowl the first over for India Women.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The West Indies Women's bowling unit had a tough day in the office, struggling to contain the batting unit of India Women. The bowlers were wayward, leaking runs all over the park, and failed to exert any significant pressure on the Indian batting line-up. Karishma Ramharack was one of the few bright spots, managing to pick up two wickets, while Deandra Dottin chipped in with one scalp. Unfortunately, the rest of the bowling attack failed to make any meaningful impact, and the fielding was also a letdown, with a few misfields and dropped catches.

Hayley Matthews might be ruing her decision to put India Women in to bat first after winning the toss! India Women have come out all guns blazing, taking full advantage of the Power Play to score a blistering 50 runs. The opening duo of Smriti Mandhana and Uma Chetry set the tone, but it was the second-wicket partnership between Jemimah Rodrigues and Smriti Mandhana that really took the game away from the West Indies. The pair added a scintillating 81 runs in just 44 balls, with Jemimah Rodrigues being the aggressor. Rodrigues went on to score a magnificent 73 runs before finally getting dismissed in the final over. Smriti Mandhana also brought up a well-deserved half-century, helping India Women post a formidable total. The West Indies will now have to regroup and come up with a solid plan to chase down this imposing target.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for play to begin. The umpires walk out to the middle followed by the players of West Indies Women led by Hayley Matthews. For India Women, Smriti Mandhana walks out along with Uma Chetry to open the innings. To open the attack with the ball for West Indies Women, it will be Chinelle Henry.

The players from both teams, West Indies Women and India Women have gathered on the field, standing shoulder to shoulder with the match officials. First, it will be the National Anthem of the West Indies, "Rally Round the West Indies". Following this, the Indian National Anthem, "Jana Gana Mana", will be played, evoking a sense of pride and unity among the Indian team and their supporters.

The skipper of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says they would have bowled as well. Mentions that they will look to take this as a fresh game and not think about what has happened in the past. Adds that they will be looking to play on the front foot and will look to post a solid total on board.

The skipper of West Indies Women, Hayley Matthews says they will bowl first. Mentions that playing here is a good opportunity for the young guns to have an outing against a top side. Reckons that they will have to be at their best as India are a very competitive side.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Uma Chetry, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Sajana S, Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Saima Thakor, Titas Sadhu, Renuka Singh Thakur.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Qiana Joseph, Shemaine Campbelle (WK), Deandra Dottin, Chinelle Henry, Shabika Gajnabi, Afy Fletcher, Zaida James, Mandy Mangru, Karishma Ramharack, Shamilia Connell.
TOSS - The coin is flipped, HEADS is the call from Hayley Matthews and it lands in favor of West Indies Women. The skipper of West Indies Women, Hayley Matthews has decided to BOWL first.

On the other hand, the West Indies Women's team, led by the seasoned Hayley Matthews, will be looking to break their drought in India, where they haven't won a T20I in recent years. Matthews will be banking on the likes of Deandra Dottin, the "World Boss," along with Shabika Gajnabi, Rashada Williams, and others to turn the tide in their favor. With the Indian team looking to bounce back from their recent setbacks and the West Indies seeking to make a statement, this series promises to be an exciting and closely contested affair. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Despite the disappointing results, India Women has shown faith in some of the young performers, with Minnu Mani, Priya Mishra, and Saima Thakor earning spots in the squad for this series. However, the surprise omission of Shafali Verma and Arundhati Reddy continues to raise eyebrows. Indian skipper Harmanpreet Kaur will rely on the experienced trio of Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, and Richa Ghosh to provide the necessary firepower and support.

India Women is set to face the West Indies Women team in the 1st T20I of the 3-match series. India Women comes into this series on the back of a dismal performance against Australia Women, where they were swept 3-0 and failed to pose a significant challenge to the Aussies.
... MATCHDAY ...

After a humbling 3-0 ODI series defeat against Australia Women, Team India is back home, determined to bounce back in a three-match T20I series against West Indies Women. The stage is set at the Dr. DY Patil University Sports Ground in Navi Mumbai, and the Women in Blue will be itching to reclaim their winning touch. The ODI series exposed India's struggles under pressure, but skipper Harmanpreet Kaur is confident her side can turn things around. With the spotlight firmly on her leadership, she’ll expect her teammates to step up when it matters most. Smriti Mandhana, fresh off an excellent century in the last ODI, will be India’s key weapon at the top. Meanwhile, Shafali Verma, who missed the ODI series, has been omitted again and it will be interesting to see the opening combination of the team. Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh bring flair and finishing firepower, while the dependable Deepti Sharma remains India's trump card with her all-round brilliance. India’s bowlers, led by Renuka Singh Thakur and Saima Thakor, need to deliver breakthroughs in crunch moments while they can also turn to the experienced spinner, Radha Yadav. The bench is brimming with talent and the likes of Nandini Kashyap, Sajana S, and Raghvi Bist getting called up, gives the hosts a chance to experiment with combinations as they prepare for the big stage ahead. On the other side, West Indies Women enter the series without having played a single game since their ICC T20 World Cup semi-final heartbreak against New Zealand. Adding to their woes, they’ll miss the experienced Stafanie Taylor. Yet, this is a team that thrives on unpredictability. Hayley Matthews, a natural leader and a dynamic all-rounder, will carry their hopes alongside the ever-dangerous Deandra Dottin, who can win matches single-handedly. The likes of Shemaine Campbelle and Aaliyah Alleyne strengthen the batting, while Chinelle Henry and Karishma Ramharack provide solid options with the ball. Both teams have firepower and match-winners, but India holds a slight edge, having beaten the Windies 13 times in T20Is compared to the visitors’ 8 wins. That said, cricket’s charm lies in its unpredictability, and it all comes down to who handles the pressure better on the day. Who are you rooting for in this battle of grit and glory?
